name: carddemo-ui
description: React 19 and TypeScript single-page application that replaces the AWS CardDemo 3270/BMS online screens with 21 browser routes.

carddemoDependencyRationale.$note: Project-owned metadata that npm ignores. package.json is strict JSON and admits no comments, so the WHY that every other file in this tree carries as an inline comment lives here instead, keyed by the exact dependency entry it explains. Assumptions: each label key retains its trailing colon, so that the four canonical labels defined in docs/CODE_DOCUMENTATION_STANDARD.md appear here as exactly the literal, colon-terminated strings a fixed-string audit searches for. Dropping the colon because a JSON key is already delimited would produce a variant this repository does not accept. Trade-offs: only decisions that are NOT self-evident from the version string are recorded, because restating an obvious pin would bury the two that matter.

engines.Assumptions:: the floor is a SECURITY floor and no longer a dependency floor. The dependency floor is 22.22.0, set by react-router 8.3.0 -- a direct dependency, and the highest engines.node any entry in package-lock.json declares, above the 22.12.0 the Vite and Vitest chain asks for and the ^22.13.0 eslint-plugin-jsdoc requires. This range sits ABOVE all of them because Node's 29 July 2026 release fixed eleven CVEs, three rated HIGH, and every 22.x below 22.23.2 predates all three: CVE-2026-56846 lets an HTTP/2 peer evade the maxSessionMemory accounting that bounds per-session memory, CVE-2026-56848 is a heap use-after-free in bundled nghttp2, and CVE-2026-58043 makes the Permission Model treat a granted path as a radix prefix and over-grant to sibling paths sharing leading characters. Trade-offs: the second arm is >=24.18.1 rather than the >=24.0.0 the dependency floor alone would permit, because 24.18.1 is the first release on the 24.x line carrying the same three fixes; stating >=24.0.0 beside a 22.23.2 floor would leave a range that admits a 24.x build strictly more exposed than the oldest 22.x it accepts, which is the kind of asymmetry an engines range exists to prevent. Assumptions: raising a floor for an advisory rather than for a constraint means this range EXPIRES -- it is a statement about what is patched today, so a later advisory moves it again, and the number is not to be read as a compatibility minimum.

scripts.Assumptions:: typecheck runs tsc twice because this package holds TWO disjoint TypeScript projects, and `tsc -p` checks exactly one. tsconfig.json covers the browser sources under src; tsconfig.node.json covers vite.config.ts and vitest.config.ts, which execute under Node and are granted @types/node that browser code is deliberately denied. Checking only the app project left both build-configuration files unchecked by any compiler: eslint gives them type-aware LINT rules, but eslint does not report compiler diagnostics, so a genuine type error in either one failed nothing and surfaced later as a confusing build or test failure far from its cause.
scripts.Refactoring Rationale:: contracts was ADDED as a script of its own even though `npm test` already runs the file it targets, and the duplication is deliberate. src/api/contracts.test.ts is the only build step in this repository that compares this package's typed API client layer with the six service-held OpenAPI documents it is written against, and docs/adr/ADR-006-api-and-ui.md now cites it by name as the mechanism that makes contract drift a build failure. A named script gives .github/workflows/ui-ci.yml a step whose title says what it enforces, so a reader of a failed run sees `Check API contract agreement` rather than a generic test failure among 33 others, and it gives a developer changing a service contract one command to run without waiting for jsdom to start for every screen test. Trade-offs: the path is written twice, here and in the workflow's own step, which is the cost accepted for that legibility; the file itself asserts a measured operation count so a rename that broke one caller would not leave the other silently asserting nothing.
scripts.Trade-offs:: build delegates to `npm run typecheck` instead of repeating the two tsc invocations inline. The extra npm process is accepted because a repeated command string in a file that admits no comments is a drift hazard: an editor who extends typecheck and forgets build would silently return the bundle to the unchecked state this entry exists to close. Type-checking still precedes vite build, which is the property that matters, because esbuild strips types without checking them and a bare `vite build` will happily emit a bundle containing type errors.

react-router.Alternatives Considered:: react-router-dom, which is the conventional choice and is deliberately ABSENT from this manifest. It has no release at major version 8 at all; its newest release is a thin re-export shim whose own dependency is react-router 7.18.1. Depending on it would therefore silently pin routing a full major version behind while looking like the safer, more idiomatic option. Every screen under ui/src/screens and ui/src/router.tsx import from react-router directly for this reason.
react-router.Assumptions:: the browser entry points this project needs -- BrowserRouter, Routes, Route, Navigate, useNavigate, useParams and useSearchParams -- are all exported from react-router itself at 8.x, so the companion package adds no API. Reintroducing react-router-dom would not add capability; it would only add an indirection that caps the version.

typescript.Trade-offs:: held below the newest major release on purpose. typescript-eslint 8.65.0 peer-declares typescript ">=4.8.4 <6.1.0", so TypeScript 7.x falls outside the range the type-aware lint pass accepts. Crossing that bound does not fail loudly: it stops the type-aware pass, and with it the eslint-plugin-jsdoc documentation gate that enforces Rule 1 for this package, from running at all. Compile speed is therefore traded for a documentation gate that actually executes.
typescript.Assumptions:: this pin is load-bearing and is not routine version conservatism. Raising it requires first raising typescript-eslint to a release whose peer range admits the new compiler, and confirming that `npm run lint` still reports the JSDoc rules. Bumping typescript alone leaves the manifest installable and the gate silently inert.

typescript-eslint.Assumptions:: this entry is what imposes the TypeScript ceiling recorded above, so the two versions move together and neither may be raised alone. It supplies the type-aware rule set that eslint-plugin-jsdoc's contexts are evaluated against; without a compiler inside its peer range the JSDoc gate does not run.
